question:
Match the atmospheric phenomenon with its primary measurement instrument

1. Wind Speed

2. Humidity

3. Atmospheric Pressure
solution:
The correct answer is __**1-Anemometer, 2-Hygrometer, 3-Barometer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Wind Speed (Statement 1)**: The instrument used to measure the speed of the wind is the **Anemometer**. It typically consists of **three or four cups** that rotate as the wind blows; the faster the rotation, the higher the wind speed recorded. *Hence, Statement 1 is correctly matched with Anemometer.*
 
• **Humidity (Statement 2)**: **Humidity**, which refers to the concentration of water vapor present in the air, is measured using a **Hygrometer**. This device is vital for weather forecasting as it helps determine the likelihood of precipitation or fog. *Hence, Statement 2 is correctly matched with Hygrometer.*
 
• **Atmospheric Pressure (Statement 3)**: The **Barometer** is the primary scientific instrument used to measure **atmospheric pressure**, also known as barometric pressure. Changes in air pressure measured by this tool are key indicators of shifting weather patterns, such as the arrival of storms or clear skies. *Hence, Statement 3 is correctly matched with Barometer.*
 
• **Logical Matching**: Based on the scientific application of these tools, **Option C** correctly pairs the atmospheric phenomenon with its specific measurement device. *Hence, the statement regarding the combination in Option C is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anemometer Details**:

 
 
• The first description of an anemometer was given by **Leon Battista Alberti** in **1450**.
 
• **Functions**: It measures both **wind speed** and **wind pressure**.
 
• **Types**: Common types include **Cup Anemometers**, **Vane Anemometers**, and **Hot-wire Anemometers** (used for measuring turbulent flows).
 
• **Applications**: Widely used in **meteorology**, **aviation**, and by engineers to monitor wind conditions for **wind turbines**.
 
 
 
• **Hygrometer Details**:
 
 
• Early versions were conceptualized by **Leonardo da Vinci** in **1480**, while the first practical version was created by **Horace Bénédict de Saussure** in **1783** using human hair.
 
• **Types**: Modern devices include **Electronic Hygrometers**, **Psychrometers** (wet and dry bulb thermometers), and **Dew-point Hygrometers**.
 
• **Uses**: Essential in **industrial spaces**, **greenhouses**, **museums**, and **cigar humidors** to maintain specific moisture levels.
 
 
 
• **Barometer Details**:
 
 
• The **Mercury Barometer** was invented by **Evangelista Torricelli** in the year **1643**.
 
• **Features**: There are two main types: **Mercury Barometers** and **Aneroid Barometers** (which do not use liquid and are more portable).
 
• **Units**: Pressure is often recorded in **millibars (mb)**, **hectopascals (hPa)**, or **inches of mercury (inHg)**. Standard sea-level pressure is approximately **1013.25 hPa**.
 
 
 
• **Other Meteorological Instruments**:
 
 
• **Wind Vane**: Also known as a weathercock, it is used to determine the **direction** from which the wind is blowing.
 
• **Rain Gauge**: Also called an **Ombrometer** or **Udometer**, it measures the amount of **liquid precipitation** (rain) over a specific **time interval**.
 
• **Thermometer**: Used to measure the **ambient air temperature**, often using the **Celsius** or **Fahrenheit** scale.
